emergency.label: No heat or no AC?
emergency.detail: No-heat and no-cooling calls across {{area}} get priority, evenings and weekends included.

maintenance_plan.name: Tune-up plan
maintenance_plan.pitch: Two visits a year (cooling in spring, heating in fall), priority scheduling when it's busy and a discount on repairs. A lot of breakdowns start as a dirty coil, a weak capacitor or a clogged drain line, and a tune-up catches those.

subheads: We find the problem, give you a flat price and fix most issues on the first visit.
Air conditioners, furnaces, heat pumps and ductless systems for homes across {{area}}.
We run a load calculation before we quote a new system, so you don't pay for one that's too big or too small.

services.name: AC repair
services.short: Warm air, weak airflow, iced-up lines or a unit that won't shut off.
services.long: We check the whole system, from the thermostat to the outdoor unit, before we name a cause. Common fixes like capacitors, contactors, fan motors and clogged drain lines are usually done the same visit from parts on the truck. If it's low on refrigerant, we find the leak before we add more.
bullets: Capacitor, contactor and fan motor replacement
Refrigerant leak detection and repair
Frozen coil and clogged condensate line fixes
All major brands

services.name: Furnace and heating repair
services.short: No heat, short cycling, odd smells or a furnace that keeps shutting off.
services.long: Most no-heat calls come down to an igniter, flame sensor, pressure switch or blower motor. We test the system, check for carbon monoxide and give you a flat price before replacing anything.
bullets: Gas and electric furnaces, boilers and heat pumps
Igniter, flame sensor and blower repairs
Carbon monoxide and heat exchanger checks
Thermostat diagnosis and replacement

services.name: Tune-ups and maintenance
services.short: Spring AC and fall furnace tune-ups that catch small problems early.
services.long: A tune-up is a cleaning and a checkup. We clean the coils and burners, test the electrical parts and safety controls, check refrigerant pressures and clear the drain line. You get a written list of anything wearing out, with no pressure to fix it that day.
bullets: Coil, burner and drain line cleaning
Electrical and safety control testing
Refrigerant and airflow checks
Filter change and written condition report

services.name: AC replacement
services.short: New central air sized with a load calculation, usually installed in a day.
services.long: We size the new system with a Manual J load calculation instead of copying the old unit's size. Most replacements take one day, including the line set, pad, electrical disconnect and startup testing. We handle the permit and register the warranty.
bullets: Manual J load calculation before we quote
Two or three options with efficiency ratings explained
Permit, startup testing and haul-away included
Manufacturer warranty registered for you

services.name: Furnace replacement
services.short: Gas furnaces and air handlers installed with a permit and inspection.
services.long: If your furnace is 15 to 20 years old or needs a repair that costs more than it's worth, we'll price a replacement next to the repair so you can compare. We handle the venting, gas connection, permit and inspection.
bullets: 80% and 95%+ efficiency gas furnaces
Venting and condensate changes for high-efficiency units
Carbon monoxide test at startup
Old unit removed and recycled

services.name: Heat pumps
services.short: One system that cools in summer and heats in winter, including cold-climate models.
services.long: A heat pump moves heat instead of burning fuel, so one system handles both heating and cooling. In colder areas we pair it with a gas furnace as backup or install a cold-climate model. We'll show you how operating costs compare with what you have now.
bullets: Ducted and ductless heat pumps
Dual-fuel setups with a gas furnace backup
Cold-climate models rated for low temperatures
Utility rebate paperwork where available

services.name: Ductless mini-splits
services.short: Heating and cooling for additions, garages and rooms the ducts don't reach.
services.long: Mini-splits mount on the wall or ceiling and connect to a small outdoor unit through a hole about three inches wide. Each room gets its own control, and there's no ductwork to build. Most single-room installs take a day.
bullets: Single and multi-zone systems
Wall, ceiling cassette and slim ducted indoor units
Line set covers for a clean exterior
A good fit for additions, sunrooms and finished garages

services.name: Indoor air quality and ductwork
services.short: Better filters, humidity control and duct repairs for dusty or uneven rooms.
services.long: If some rooms are always too hot or too cold, or the house is dusty no matter how often you clean, the ductwork is often the cause. We test airflow, seal and repair leaky ducts and add filtration or humidity control where it helps.
bullets: Media filters and air cleaners
Whole-home humidifiers and dehumidifiers
Duct sealing, repair and new runs
Room-by-room airflow testing

trust.badges_hint: NATE certification and manufacturer dealer status (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Rheem and others) are what homeowners recognize. ACCA membership, BBB accreditation and local utility rebate program participation are also worth showing. Every technician who handles refrigerant must hold EPA 608, so treat it as a baseline, not a selling point. The certifications listed are examples; keep only the ones the business holds and swap in its actual brand program (for example Rheem Pro Partner).

faqs.q: How much does a new AC or furnace cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the size of the house, the efficiency you choose and whether the ductwork needs changes. Central AC replacements commonly run $5,000 to $12,000 installed, and gas furnaces $3,000 to $7,500. Heat pumps vary more. We quote in writing after measuring your house, with a few options to compare.

faqs.q: Should I repair or replace my system?
faqs.a: A common rule of thumb: if the system is over 12 to 15 years old and the repair costs more than a third of a new one, replacement usually makes more sense. Frequent breakdowns and rising bills point the same way. We'll price both so you can decide.

faqs.q: My AC uses R-22. Can it still be fixed?
faqs.a: R-22 hasn't been produced or imported in the US since 2020, so what's left is expensive. Electrical and fan repairs are still worth doing. A refrigerant leak on an R-22 system is usually the point where replacement makes more sense.

faqs.q: What should I check before I call?
faqs.a: Make sure the thermostat is set to heat or cool and has fresh batteries, the filter isn't clogged and the breaker for the system hasn't tripped. For a furnace, check that the power switch near it is on. If none of that fixes it, call us.

faqs.q: How often should I change my filter?
faqs.a: Check it monthly. Basic 1-inch filters usually need changing every one to three months, more often with pets or heavy use. Thicker 4 to 5 inch media filters typically last six months to a year.

faqs.q: What size system do I need?
faqs.a: That comes from a load calculation (Manual J), which looks at square footage, insulation, windows and which way the house faces. Copying the size of the old unit is how a lot of homes end up with oversized systems that cycle on and off and leave the air clammy.

faqs.q: How long does a new system install take?
faqs.a: Most AC or furnace replacements take one day. A full system with both, or one that needs new ductwork, can take two to three days. We give you the schedule when we quote.

faqs.q: Do you offer financing or rebates?
faqs.a: Yes, financing is available on new systems with approved credit. Many utilities and manufacturers offer rebates on high-efficiency equipment, and we'll check which ones apply in {{area}} and help with the paperwork.
